newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech shares steady as key investors wait-and-see.
newsitem.headline: Czech shares steady as key investors wait-and-see.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange continued to suffer from the absence of foreign investors on Thursday, edging up slightly on gains to a couple of major shares.

The PX50 index closed 0.7 points higher at 509.3, but analysts said the market was still plagued by small volumes as foreign investors, put off by a lack of transparency and poor shareholder rights, remain on the sidelines.
"We're just not seeing any volumes and I doubt we will until key investors return to the market," said one trader.

Foreign investors have long-complained about a lack of regulation of the Czech equities market, that allows some 70 percent of trading to occur off-market where information on volumes, prices and counterparties is opaque at best.
"Other markets in the area are doing better because at least there, an investor who's not on the ground feels they have a chance," the trader added.
Overall on Thursday, 1.175 million shares changed hands on turnover of some 985.4 million crowns.
Komercni Banka and engineering concern Skoda were two blue chips that fared well on the day, posting modest gains of 11 crowns and 17 crowns respectively.
